saturation.reason: Wave 6 finds a new current false negative with mandatory local/regional authority beneficiaries (CIRCBIO-04) and a current promotion gap already discovered internally (Co-create NEB), plus additional current conditional-partner/source-family gaps.

currentFindings.title: HORIZON-CL6-2026-01-CIRCBIO-04 · Demonstrating and deploying innovative collection, sorting-for-reuse and repair systems for textiles at city/region level
currentFindings.funding: Horizon Europe Innovation Action; EUR 10 million topic budget; around EUR 5 million per project
currentFindings.eligibilityEvidence: The topic requires at least nine distinct regional/local authorities as beneficiaries: three demonstration cities/regions and six replication cities/regions.

currentFindings.title: Co-create NEB · Open Call 2027
currentFindings.funding: Grant up to EUR 49,300; co-funding EUR 8,700; total project budget EUR 58,000
currentFindings.eligibilityEvidence: Co-create NEB requires a consortium of 2-4 partners with at least one municipality, region or affiliated entity and targets place-based public-space transformation through municipal collaboration.

conditionalCurrentGaps.note: Strongest residual LIFE CET municipal fit; local authorities are explicitly within the public-authority scope, but a municipality is not established as a mandatory beneficiary in every proposal.
Integrated renovation one-stop-shops rely on strong territorial partnerships including local/regional authorities; no universal mandatory municipal beneficiary was established.

conditionalCurrentGaps.title: Developing managed aquifer recharge techniques (MAR) in a rural context
conditionalCurrentGaps.note: The topic requires the multi-actor approach and adequate involvement of relevant stakeholders including local authorities, but does not require a municipality to be a beneficiary.
The topic targets tools for local/regional authorities and strongly recommends involvement of road authorities; no mandatory municipal beneficiary condition was established.
CIVITAS CSA is explicitly city/local-regional in delivery and capacity building, but a mandatory municipal beneficiary was not established.
Public authorities are among programme target organisations, but municipality fit requires an interregional consortium and shared/complementary smart-specialisation priorities.

routeAndLifecycleControls.funding: EUR 77 million Specific Action; EUR 0.8-7.5 million per project; up to 90% EU co-financing
routeAndLifecycleControls.note: The 2 October deadline is for national Managing Authorities to submit to the Commission. No dedicated Italian selection notice clearly mapping this action was confirmed in this sweep.
Upstream contractor procurement is complete/under award lifecycle; no downstream municipal EOI was confirmed published as of 8 September.

Not a runtime miss on 8 September because the call has not opened. Article 11 status is required for the primary city-under-review role; peer reviewers can represent any EU urban authority with relevant experience.

internalReviewControls.note: ANCI discovery duplicates for Amianto Edifici Pubblici, Mercati rionali and Toscana Diffusa remain in internal_review, but the canonical Regione Toscana/Sviluppo Toscana opportunities are already public. This is queue noise/dedup, not a promotion gap.
City-to-City Exchanges is already public as rolling_open while additional fragments of the same official page remain in internal_review. Again this is dedup noise rather than missing publication.

positiveOrNegativeControls.note: Connect NEB is open in the same EIT call, but its single-beneficiary target list focuses on community organisations, NGOs, social innovators, artists/designers, SMEs and research groups; no municipality requirement supports automatic promotion.
Local-authority involvement is required as a relevant stakeholder under the multi-actor approach, but beneficiary status is not mandatory; preserve this distinction in future rules.
